title: Axial $U(1)$ Symmetry Breaking in Hot QCD: From Topology to the Chiral Phase Transition
summary: Heating matter can restore symmetries spontaneously broken at low temperature. The axial $U(1)$ symmetry of quantum chromodynamics (QCD) is different: it is present in the classical theory with massless quarks but is broken upon quantization by the axial anomaly. The anomaly persists at every temperature, yet its observable effects can weaken. Can hot matter nevertheless behave as though this symmetry were restored at long distances?
